description: A common mental health condition causing persistent sadness, loss of interest, and inability to carry out daily activities. Very common in India but severely underdiagnosed due to stigma.
symptoms: persistent sadness or empty feeling for more than 2 weeks
loss of interest in activities once enjoyed
changes in appetite — eating too much or too little
sleep disturbances — too much or too little sleep
fatigue and loss of energy
feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt
difficulty thinking, concentrating or making decisions
thoughts of death or suicide
india_context: Depression affects 56 million Indians. Highly stigmatised. Patients often present with physical complaints like body pain and headache rather than emotional symptoms. ASHA workers are trained in basic mental health support under NMHP.
when_to_seek_help: If symptoms last more than 2 weeks or there are any thoughts of self-harm, see a doctor immediately. Depression is a medical condition, not a character weakness.
what_helps: Talking to a trusted person, regular sleep schedule, daily exercise even 20 minutes walking, sunlight exposure, social connection, professional therapy (CBT), medication if prescribed by psychiatrist.
treatment: Psychotherapy especially CBT is most evidence-based. Antidepressants (SSRIs like Escitalopram, Sertraline) if prescribed by psychiatrist. Do NOT start or stop antidepressants without doctor guidance. Takes 4-6 weeks to see full effect.
helplines_india: iCall (TISS Mumbai): 9152987821 — Monday to Saturday 8am to 10pm
source: WHO mhGAP guidelines, NIMHANS India, Ministry of Health NMHP

description: Excessive, persistent worry and fear that is difficult to control and interferes with daily activities. Most common mental health condition globally and in India.
symptoms: excessive worrying that is hard to control
feeling restless or on edge constantly
muscle tension
difficulty concentrating
sleep problems particularly difficulty falling asleep
rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath during anxiety episodes
sweating and trembling
avoiding situations that trigger anxiety
india_context: Anxiety is often expressed as physical symptoms in India including chest tightness, palpitations, and headache. Frequently confused with cardiac or gastrointestinal conditions. Exam stress and financial pressure are major triggers for Indian youth.
when_to_seek_help: When anxiety interferes with work, relationships or daily function consistently for more than 6 months, or when panic attacks occur.
what_helps: Diaphragmatic deep breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, regular exercise, limiting caffeine and alcohol, consistent sleep schedule, mindfulness meditation.
treatment: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) is gold standard and most effective. SSRIs if medication needed. Benzodiazepines only for very short-term use due to dependence risk. PRESCRIPTION REQUIRED for all medications.
source: WHO mhGAP guidelines, American Psychiatric Association DSM-5

description: Overwhelming mental and physical exhaustion from prolonged exposure to demanding situations. Recognised by WHO as an occupational phenomenon in ICD-11. Very common among students, farmers, healthcare workers and urban professionals in India.
symptoms: extreme fatigue that does not improve with rest
feeling detached, cynical or negative about work and life
difficulty completing tasks that were previously easy
frequent headaches and body pain
frequent illness due to lowered immunity
irritability and short temper
loss of motivation and sense of purpose
feeling helpless or trapped
india_context: Farmer burnout and suicide is a major crisis in India particularly in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Student burnout during board exams and entrance test preparation is extremely common. Agricultural helpline: Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551.
self_care_steps: Identify and reduce stressors where possible
Set clear boundaries between work and personal time
Regular physical activity even 20 minutes walking daily
Maintain consistent sleep and wake time
Stay connected with supportive friends and family
Limit news and social media to defined times
Practice brief mindfulness or prayer for 10 minutes daily
Take regular short breaks during work
when_to_seek_help: When self-care strategies do not help after 3 weeks, or when symptoms of depression or anxiety appear, seek professional support.
source: WHO ICD-11 Burnout Classification Z73.0, National Mental Health Programme India

description: Suicidal thoughts or self-harm intentions are always a serious crisis requiring immediate support. India has approximately 230000 suicide deaths annually making it one of the highest globally. Most suicides are preventable with timely intervention.
warning_signs: talking about wanting to die or to kill themselves
looking for ways to access means to harm themselves
talking about being a burden to family or others
increasing use of alcohol or drugs
withdrawing completely from friends and family
sudden calmness after a period of depression (may indicate decision made)
saying goodbye to people as if they will not see them again
what_to_do: Take all talk of suicide seriously — never dismiss it as attention seeking
Ask directly and calmly: Are you thinking about suicide? — asking does not plant the idea
Listen without judgment and without minimising their pain
Remove access to means if safely possible — medicines, sharp objects, ropes
Stay with the person — do not leave them alone
Call a helpline together or take them to the nearest hospital emergency
Follow up regularly after a crisis — isolation increases risk
immediate_helplines: Vandrevala Foundation: 1860-2662-345 — 24 hours, free, multilingual Hindi English
iCall TISS: 9152987821 — Monday to Saturday 8am to 10pm
india_context: Suicide rates are highest among young adults aged 18-30 and farmers in India. Pesticide ingestion is a common method in rural areas. Restricting access to pesticides reduces rural suicide rates significantly. Seeking mental health help is not weakness.
source: WHO Suicide Prevention Guidelines LIVE LIFE, NIMHANS, iCall TISS

description: Depression occurring after childbirth affecting mothers and sometimes fathers. Distinct from normal baby blues which last only 2 weeks. Very common but rarely discussed in India due to cultural expectations on new mothers.
symptoms: persistent sadness, emptiness or hopelessness lasting more than 2 weeks after birth
inability to bond with or care for the baby
withdrawing from family and friends
loss of appetite or overeating
inability to sleep even when baby sleeps
overwhelming fatigue
feeling like a failure as a mother
in severe cases: thoughts of harming self or baby
india_context: Postpartum depression affects 22% of Indian mothers but is massively underdiagnosed. Cultural pressure to be a perfect happy mother prevents women from seeking help. Family and husband support are critical protective factors.
when_to_seek_help: Any depression symptoms lasting more than 2 weeks after birth, or any thoughts of harming self or baby, require immediate medical help. This is a medical condition caused by hormonal changes, not a character failure.
treatment: Psychotherapy and social support are first line. Antidepressants safe during breastfeeding are available if needed (prescription required). Partner and family involvement in care is essential.
source: WHO Maternal Mental Health Guidelines, FOGSI India
